paper.title: LLM-generated implementations of classic graph algorithms

plan_review.notes: Hand-written plan for run-plan PoC (Planner skipped).

payload.plan_summary: Engineer implements 5 classic graph algorithms from specifications and test data. Reviewer validates correctness through systematic testing.
payload.objective: Evaluate Engineer's ability to implement DFS, BFS, Dijkstra, Floyd-Warshall, and Kruskal from specifications and test data.

phases.title: Install Python dependencies
phases.goal: Install networkx and numpy into the paper venv.

phases.title: Engineer implements 5 graph algorithms
phases.goal: Engineer writes Python implementations of 5 algorithms and returns code + metrics in metrics.json.
phases.planned_actions: Engineer generates graph_algorithms.py. The runner validates it with run_graph.py.

dfs.output: list of visited nodes in traversal order
dfs.constraints: iterative or recursive; must visit all reachable nodes; graph structure in test_data.json

bfs.output: list of visited nodes in breadth-first order
bfs.constraints: must use queue data structure; visit nodes level-by-level; graph structure in test_data.json

dijkstra.input: weighted graph dict {node: [(neighbor, weight)]}, source node (int)
dijkstra.output: dict {node: shortest_distance}, or tuple (distances, paths) if paths requested
dijkstra.constraints: non-negative weights only; use priority queue; return shortest path distances from source to all reachable nodes

kruskal.input: list of edges [(u, v, weight)] for undirected graph, node count (int)
kruskal.output: tuple (mst_edges, total_weight) where mst_edges is list of (u, v, weight)
kruskal.constraints: minimum spanning tree (acyclic, minimum total weight); use union-find or Kruskal's algorithm; no edge is repeated

floyd_warshall.output: dict {source: {target: shortest_distance}} for all node pairs
floyd_warshall.constraints: support disconnected node pairs using infinity; match all-pairs shortest-path distances

phases.title: Validate Engineer algorithms against benchmark graphs
phases.goal: Run each implemented algorithm through run_graph.py and capture CapturedMetric JSON.
phases.planned_actions: Execute run_graph.py for each algorithm using Engineer graph_algorithms.py.

assumptions: Engineer generates implementations of 5 algorithms (dfs, bfs, dijkstra, floyd_warshall, kruskal).
Engineer receives test_data.json (input graphs only: nodes, edges, weights, adjacency lists).
Algorithm specs embedded in plan: input/output format and constraints for each algorithm.
Engineer writes single artifact: metrics.json containing code segment + test results for observability.
constraints: Engineer timeout: 10 minutes (code generation + local testing).
No external ground truth exposed to Engineer during construction.
risks: DFS/BFS order may differ from NetworkX if adjacency lists are built differently.
Dijkstra: Engineer may forget non-negative weight assumption.
Kruskal: Union-find implementation bugs are common.
Floyd-Warshall must represent unreachable pairs consistently.
execution: Setup, Engineer writes graph_algorithms.py, runner validates with run_graph.py, Reviewer grades against benchmark ground truth.
repo_usage: Engineer reads staged graphs.json without embedded ground_truth answers.
run_graph.py executes Engineer code and writes per-algorithm metric JSON under results/synthetic_graph/.
engineer_notes: You receive graphs.json with test graphs (nodes, edges, adjacency lists).
Algorithm specs are in the plan above: input format, output format, and constraints for each of the 5 algorithms.
Implement all 5 algorithms: dfs, bfs, dijkstra, floyd_warshall, kruskal.
The runner validates implementations with run_graph.py after construction.
